newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shares end firm in rally led by Chispas.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shares end firm in rally led by Chispas.

text.p: Chilean blue chips on Thursday closed more than one percent higher in light trade, with the market led by a rally in the Chispa group of power investment companies, dealers said.
The bolsa is closed Friday for a public holiday and will reopen Monday at 0930 local (1430 GMT).
The weighted IPSA index ended up 1.29 percent at 132.23 points.
The general IGPA index gained 0.56 percent to 5,613.53 points.
Turnover fell to 8.2 billion pesos from over 11 billion pesos Wednesday.
The gains came amid fresh rumours of an interest rate cut by the Chilean central bank, triggering a rebound after two weeks of profit-taking.
"We all know an interest rate cut is the next thing to come, so that could well account for today's rise," said David Hurd, head of research at Merrill Lynch.
The Chispa group of companies, which control energy group Enersis, rallied amid speculation that a second bidder may emerge to raise the offer of 220 pesos made by Spain's Endesa, said dealers.
Other traders said that they doubted the rumors were true, adding that turnover in the Chispa stocks was low.
Among the Chispa stocks, Chispados ended up 7.14 percent at 180 pesos, while Almendros rose 6.51 percent to 180 pesos.
Among declining issues, Cemento Melon SA closed down 3.16 percent at 46 pesos, and forestry company Inforsa which dropped 2.33 percent at 63 pesos.
